summary: idnna 0.2.0: typosquat with base64-obfuscated install-time dropper fetching remote binary
details: The pypi distribution 'idnna' is a one-character typosquat of the widely used 'idna' package. Its setup.py registers a custom install cmdclass whose body is stored as a base64 blob and executed via exec(compile(...)) at install time. On Linux, the decoded payload downloads a binary from https://github.com/totti2188/8gp1Q7iZD3h4VW/releases/download/v1.3A/something to a path under /tmp, chmods it 0755, and spawns it detached from the pip process. No hash or signature verification is performed, and the GitHub account hosting the binary is unrelated to the package's stated purpose ('HTTP client utilities'). The shipped Python code is a stub package directory named 'djangoo' containing only a trivial hello() function, confirming that the package has no legitimate functionality and exists solely to deliver the install-time payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
